chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Musa ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Razi from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

Some of his companions asked him about using the siwak (tooth-stick) during the month of Ramadan. He said, 'It is permissible.' Some of them said, 'Indeed, the moisture of the siwak enters the stomach (jawf).' He said, 'What do you say about the wet siwak, whose moisture enters the throat?' He said, 'The water used for rinsing the mouth (madhmadha) is wetter than the wet siwak.'

If a speaker says, 'There is no choice but to use water for rinsing the mouth because of the Sunnah,' then there is no choice but to use the siwak because of the Sunnah that Gabriel (peace be upon him) brought to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

As for what he mentioned (may God have mercy on him) regarding the ruling of snuffing (su'oot) and enema (huqna), it has already passed in what was mentioned before, so there is no basis for repeating it.
And the woman does not sit in the water.

key_terms.الْجَوْف: The stomach or cavity of the body

ai.seo_question: Is using siwak permissible while fasting in Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of using the siwak during Ramadan by employing a logical analogy (qiyas) with water for rinsing the mouth, arguing that if the wetness of water does not break the fast, neither does that of the siwak. He grounds this ruling in the Prophetic Sunnah transmitted by Gabriel, reinforcing the practice's spiritual and physical benefits. The narration concludes by dismissing redundant discussions on snuffing and enema, while adding a specific juristic note that a woman does not break her fast by sitting in water.
